title: Rigveda 4.27: To Soma and the eagle
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 4.27: To Soma and the eagle: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 4.27 is a hymn of 5 verses addressed to Soma and the eagle. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 4, the family book of Vāmadeva. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 286r-287r. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_text: <sup>1</sup>garbhe̱ nu sann anv e̍ṣām avedam a̱haṁ de̱vānā̱ṁ jani̍māni̱ viśvā̍ | śa̱tam mā̱ pura̱ āya̍sīr arakṣa̱nn adha̍ śye̱no ja̱vasā̱ nir a̍dīyam ||
translation.text: <sup>1</sup>I, As I lay within the womb, considered all generations of these Gods in order. A hundred iron fortresses confined me but forth I flew with rapid speed a Falcon.

translation.original_ref: RV 4.27.2-4 (aṣṭaka 3, adhyāya 6, varga 16); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 286v
translation.original_text:
2na ghā̱ sa mām apa̱ joṣa̍ṁ jabhārā̱bhīm ā̍sa̱ tvakṣa̍sā vī̱rye̍ṇa | ī̱rmā pura̍ṁdhir ajahā̱d arā̍tīr u̱ta vātā̍m̐ atara̱c chūśu̍vānaḥ ||
3ava̱ yac chye̱no asva̍nī̱d adha̱ dyor vi yad yadi̱ vāta̍ ū̱huḥ pura̍ṁdhim | sṛ̱jad yad a̍smā̱ ava̍ ha kṣi̱paj jyāṁ kṛ̱śānu̱r astā̱ mana̍sā bhura̱ṇyan ||
4ṛ̱ji̱pya ī̱m indrā̍vato̱ na bhu̱jyuṁ śye̱no ja̍bhāra bṛha̱to adhi̱ ṣṇoḥ | a̱ntaḥ pa̍tat pata̱try a̍sya pa̱rṇam adha̱ yāma̍ni̱ prasi̍tasya̱ tad veḥ ||
translation.text:
2Not at his own free pleasure did he bear me: he conquered with his strength and manly courage. Straightway the Bold One left the fiends behind him and passed the winds as he grew yet more mighty.
3When with loud cry from heaven down sped the Falcon, thence hasting like the wind he bore the Bold One. Then, wildly raging in his mind, the archer Kr̥iṣanu aimed and loosed the string to strike him.
4The Falcon bore him from heaven's lofty summit as the swift car of Indra's Friend bore Bhujyu. Then downward hither fell a flying feather of the Bird hasting forward in his journey.

translation.original_text: <sup>5</sup>adha̍ śve̱taṁ ka̱laśa̱ṁ gobhi̍r a̱ktam ā̍pipyā̱nam ma̱ghavā̍ śu̱kram andha̍ḥ | a̱dhva̱ryubhi̱ḥ praya̍ta̱m madhvo̱ agra̱m indro̱ madā̍ya̱ prati̍ dha̱t piba̍dhyai̱ śūro̱ madā̍ya̱ prati̍ dha̱t piba̍dhyai ||
translation.text: <sup>5</sup>And now let Maghavan accept the beaker, white, filled with milk, filled with the shining liquid; The best of sweet meath which the priests have offered: that Indra to his joy may drink, the Hero, that he may take and drink it to his rapture.
